1.q: to the outer sanctuary gate that faced east
1.note: Alternate translation: [to the outer sanctuary gate on the east side of the temple]

2.note: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [no one will open it]
See how you translated this in Ezekiel 8:4.

3.q: He will enter by way of the gate’s portico and go out the same way
3.note: He will enter the courtyard through another gate and then sit in the portico of the east gate and eat.

covering in front of an entrance with columns or posts for support. In this case, the portico opens into the courtyard and is between the entrance to the temple and the inside of the gate. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 8:16.
Alternate translation: [in front of Yahweh] or [in the presence of Yahweh]

4.note: This could mean: (1) “Then the man” or (2) “Then Yahweh.”
The word “behold” here shows that Ezekiel was surprised by what he saw.
See how you translated this in Ezekiel 1:28.
See how you translated this same phrase, “fell to my face,” in 43:3.

5.note: “pay attention to” or “think about.” Translate as you translated “fix your mind on” in Ezekiel 40:4.
Alternate translation: [all the instructions about the house of Yahweh]

6.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

6.q: Let all of your disgusting actions be enough for you
6.note: Alternate translation: [Your disgusting actions have been more than enough for you] or [You have done far too many disgusting deeds]
See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:9.

The phrase **to a rebellion** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [to a house of rebellion]

7.note: The phrase **And they broke** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [And you broke]

This could mean: (1) that it was by doing these **abominations** that the Israelites broke the covenant. Alternate translation: [by all your abominations] (2) that the Israelites broke the covenant in addition to committing the **abominations**. Alternate translation: [in addition to all your abominations]

10.q: went far from me … wandered away from me, going after their idols
10.note: The way a person lives is spoken of as walking on a path. Alternate translation: [stopped worshiping me … stopped doing what I wanted them to do. Instead, they worshiped their idols]

11.note: Alternate translation: [will be the servants in my temple]

11.q: watching the gates of the house
11.note: Alternate translation: [performing guard duty at the gates of the house]

11.q: they will stand before the people and serve them
11.note: Alternate translation: [these Levites will stand before the people, so that they can serve the people]

Here, the word **And** could introduce: (1) some of the ways in which the Levites must “lift up their iniquity” (44:10). Alternate translation: [So, they shall be] (2) what the Levites are still allowed to do despite having to “lift up their iniquity” (44:10). Alternate translation: [And yet, they shall be]

12.q: became stumbling blocks for sin for the house of Israel
12.note: A person who causes another person to sin is spoken of as if he were something on a path over which people stumble. Alternate translation: [became people who caused the house of Israel to sin]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

12.q: I will lift up my hand to swear an oath
12.note: In those days a person would raise his right hand to show that he realized that God would punish him if he did not do what he swore to do. See how you translated these words in Ezekiel 20:6. Alternate translation: [I will solemnly swear]
Alternate translation: [that I will punish them]

12.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
12.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **punishment**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [I will certainly punish them]

13.note: “I will not permit them to come near.” Yahweh does not want them to come to him the way a servant comes to a king to receive commands, as the descendants of Zadok will do (Ezekiel 40:46).

13.q: will bear their reproach and their guilt
13.note: Alternate translation: [will be ashamed and suffer when I punish them]
“the disgusting things you do.” God was angry because the people were worshiping idols and false gods. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:9.

14.note: people who guard or take care of something
This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [that they need to do in it]

15.q: those sons of Zadok who fulfilled
15.note: Alternate translation: [who are descendants of Zadok and fulfilled]

See how you translated this in Ezekiel 9:2.

24.q: In a dispute they will stand to judge with my decrees
24.note: Alternate translation: [When people are arguing, they will be the ones who decide who is right by applying my laws]

27.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
27.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

28.note: The word “you” refers to the people of Israel and so is plural.
land that a person owns and uses to provide for the needs of his family
Alternate translation: [in the land of Israel]

30.q: every contribution, anything from all of your contributions
30.note: Alternate translation: [every gift of whatever kind from all your gifts] or [all gifts of every sort of all of your gifts]

30.q: so that blessing may rest on your house
30.note: This phrase means “so that I will bless your family and everything that belongs to you.”

31.q: or animal torn by a beast, whether bird or beast
31.note: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [or any creature that a bird or a wild animal has torn apart]
